maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: If the hon. minister lias been misrepresented, he himself is to blame because he certainly stated this sum was to be expended for the purpose of dredging. I drew attention to the fact that there is no breakwater at Fort William and he does not intend the expenditure to be limited to Port Arthur. I do not see where there can be any more dredging done m Kaministiquia river.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Is the work done directly by the department by their own dredges or under contract?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Under contract. We pay for some by the yard and some by the hour but the result is practically the same. When we pay by the hour it is for the minimum amount of work they are obliged to do.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Who are the contractors?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Dredge No. 6, Mr. A. F. Bowman ; dredge No. 1, the Great Lakes Dredging Company ; dredge ' Kingsford,' C. S. Boone.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Is this the Mr. Bowman who is a member of the local House and to whom the government gave a guarantee of a million dollars?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: No, he is a brother of that gentleman.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: What is the principle upon which the department acts in this dredging business? Some dredges are paid by the hour and some by the yard and when paid by the yard the prices are not the same. This man Bowman must be a great friend of the government. Does the dredge ' Kingsford ' belong to Mr. Boone?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Evidently the plan of the late Minister of Public Works, Mr. Tarte, of having dredges owned by the government operating all over the Dominion, and which, he claimed, would cost less than hiring dredges, is not being carried out. Mr. Boone got $10 an hour for dredging 869 hours in July and September. Yet some years ago we were told by hon. gentlemen opposite that $8 an hour was too much. Then the Great Lake Dredging Company are paid on a different principle. They were paid 8,323 yards at 90 cents; 481 yards at 45 cents ; 7,959 yards at 23 cents and 13.122 yards at 15 cents. And all this dredging was done at the same place. I notice that any number of engineers and inspectors were employed on this work, no doubt, to inspect one another. Who is the man who decides whether a dredge will be paid by the hour or the yard and what prices shall be paid by the yard. Here is another dredge, Dredge No. 5, which I suppose belongs to the Great Lakes Dredging Company. This one was paid 7,224 yards at 90 cents; 8,777 yards at 40 cents; 47,022 yards at 23 cents ; 22,623 yards at 15 cents and 444 yards at $1.25, and all done at the same place. Mr. Bowman, who is mentioned here must be a great friend of the government.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: He was in the Local House.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: There is likely to be a row in the future. Because the two governments will not work on the same dredges. He has dredge No. 6 which is employed from August 13 to October 13, 339,596 yards at 15 cents. Another one not far from the same spot, $1.25. Then I find Bowman again at 20 cents a yard. Then there is Mr. Boone with the dredge Kingsford. It is employed for 168 hours at $12-the rate seems to be increasing. Then there is a charge of 496 hours and 50 minutes-that is getting it down fine-at $10.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: That shows that we watch them closely.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext:
There seems to be a great deal of watching judging from the number of inspectors and engineers, but I am afraid there is a combination amongst the crowd. For the purposes of this work,
I suppose, Fort William and Port Arthur are considered together, because they almost join. I understand that the hon. gentleman (Mr. Hyman) is the minister in charge of those works. I would like to know who is the man representing the government who is above all these sub-engineers and inspectors and on whom the government relies. Then I would like to know on what principle the men are paid. I do not know their political leanings, but I find some labourers are paid $2.50 a day, some $2 a day and some $1.50 a day. There seems

to be no principle in the working of the department of these matters.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman is asking a question and answering it too.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: That is very clever, but I do not see it. Perhaps the minister can tell me whether there is any rule or principle that he follows in these matters. There is another question I should like to ask. I see here a charge for a quantity of timber bought from the Pigeon River Lumber Company. In such a case are tenders called for, or does the engineer or inspector in charge go to the Pigeon River Company and say : We want to get so much timber-

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: That does not come under this vote. That is for repairs to the breakwater.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: It must be all the same thing. There is only one Port Arthur.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: But there may be different kinds of work at the same place.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Will the hon. minister call my attention to the item under which this expenditure arises when we reach it ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I will try to remember.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: And will he answer my other questions now ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext:
With pleasure.. So far as the different prices for labour is concerned, the same differences have always existed. For certain surveys we must have a better class of men, men who are a little more than labourers. These are paid $2.50 a day. As to the dredging, my hon. friend seems concerned because there were so many different kinds of material at Port Arthur. I may tell him that the plans show, in places, as many as four different kinds of material at the same spot-mud and sand on top, then clay, then hard-pan and then rock. There are different prices for these different kinds of work. The department have an engineer there, a Mr. Temple. He has been in charge there for some four years. Of course, we hold him responsible. He does not fix the prices for the dredging, but he makes reports that come to the chief engineer and the deputy. As to the different prices for dredges, $10 and $12 an hour, the price Is based upon the quantity of work the several dredges can do. It is all done to a standard. As to the general policy, speaking for myself, I think it would be well if the department had a larger fleet of dredges. But the hon. gentleman must knoy^ that these dredges are very costly. A first-class dredge to-day will cost at least a quarter of a million dollars. The department have been for years asking for votes and supplying themselves with dredges of the latest pattern and able to do work at the lowest cost. But the department could not very well ask a vote
to supply dredges for all the harbours, because in some harbours a certain kind of dredge will do the best work, while others require a different dredge. I do not think the department can ever hope to be equipped with enough dredges of its own to cover all the harbours. But it is the policy of the department to increase its dredging fleet.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: How many dredges are employed at Port Arthur and Fort William ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Four.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Were they constructed especially for this work ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Where were they constructed ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Those dredges do not belong to the department. Still I am sorry I have not the information the hon. gentleman desires. We deal simply with the contractor, and, so long as the dredge comes up to the requirements of the department we are satisfied.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I was asking with a view to understanding the practicability of the department acquiring dredges. I thought that as that was the policy of the minister he would have considered that point, and would be able to tell us whether these dredges were made in this country or elsewhere.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I have not that information.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: What are the names of the other two dredges ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext:
No. 5, the 'Arthur,' and No. 6 the ' ICingsford.' No. 5 is the Great Lakes Dredging -Company's.
Mr. FOSTER, Who is the contract made with ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: My deputy tells me that it is with Mr. A. F. Bowman.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The same man ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The same man.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: We have here for dredging the ICaministiquia river, $20,939, that is to F. A. Bowman. Then we have the Great Lakes Dredging Company, $2,119. Dredging in Kaminisquia river near elevator D, $4,036 ; Great Lakes Dredging Company, $1,333. Who owns the dredge ' Kings-ford ' ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Boone.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext:
Dredging in Port Arthur harbour at new Canadian Northern Railway elevator, $14,484 ; Great Lakes Dredging Company, $18,917, making a total amount of $73,679 for dredging Port Arthur last year. This year the minister comes

[DOT]down with another estimate of $195,000 for dredging. I have no hesitation in telling the minister that he is carrying out a wrong policy, and the public is not getting service for the money expended.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman has n right to his opinion, and possibly I have a right to mine. My opinion is that the country is getting service for the money. The expenditure comes directly under the Department of the Chief Engineer, who is watching it very closely. Since I have been in charge of the department no contract has been made or arrangement of any kind [DOT]except after a report of the chief engineer.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: From what depth to what depth is the hon. gentleman dredging, both in Port Arthur and Kaministi-quia ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The average present depth varies. The intention is to give twenty-two feet of water, gradually extending it along the docks to twenty-two feet.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Could the minister give the committee an idea of the size, capacity and value of each of these dredges ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I have not the value of the dredges, because we are dealing with contractors who do the dredging. We take into consideration the amount of work a dredge can perform in a given time. When a dredge is paid $10 an hour it is supposed to be for ordinary work. If it is in mud or sand, it is 15 cents a yard, that is considered to be a fair price.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: A modern dredge -can do the mud dredging for an infinitely less price than that.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Perhaps so. The department is now looking at a new dredge that can do the work for less price ; but there is not a dredge of that kind available in Canada.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Does that include scow-age ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Yes. While a dredge is being paid $10 an hour it is working in different kiuds of material all the while, which varies in price from lOf cents per yard up to 40 cents, depending altogether upon the character of the work the dredge is [DOT]engaged in.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The reason I asked the question as to the value is this. It was stated to us in committee several years ago by a predecessor of the minister, that the department was, as stated by my hon. friend fiom Beauharnois (Mr. Bergeron), considering a proposition to construct dredges to do this work, for the reason that it could thus be more economically performed. Several years have since elapsed, and I would have thought, if that is the opinion of the department still, that the deaprtment would have made itself acquainted with the par-

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: ticulars to which I have referred respecting these dredges, because I assume they are proper dredges for undertaking this work. If they are proper dredges for this work, then it would seem that an inquiry might have been made long ago as to the value of these dredges, and the cost of acquiring dredges of a similar character, in order that the saving spoken of by the hon. gentleman's predecessor might lie effected. The minister will agree that in that aspect of the question it would have been proper for the government to obtain some information along that line. He has spoken to us of a dredge costing $250,000. I want to find out whether any one of these dredges cost anything like that sum.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I do not think any of them did, of that character.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I think the minister will find that for the same purpose he could have bought the whole of these dredges for one-half or one-fourth of that sum. The inquiry seems to be pertinent for that reason, because if you can dredge out the harbours of Fort William and Port Arthur for 5 cents a cubic yard, there is no reason why you should be paying 15, 20 and 25 cents per cubic yard. I hope, therefore, that the minister, during the present session or at some early date, will give us some information along these lines ; because while it may be profitable to some of these gentlemen to be dredging these harbours at these rates, there is no reason in the interests of the people why that system should be pursued if it be true, as stated by the hon. gentleman's predecessor, that the work can well be done for one-third or one-fourth of the price now paid.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext:
The department can do no work at Port Arthur or at Kaministiquia until such time, as we get up-to-date dredges. If we were to attempt to do so with the present dredges, I think the hon. gentleman would say that we were not doing our full duty. If we were to acquire these dredges, I do not believe that we could do tlie work a single bit cheaper than we are doing it under the system we are pursuing at the present time. If we pursued that policy we would require immediately to spend a large amount of money on capital account for the purpose of doing the work in Port Arthur. What is to be done with the dredges afterwards ? I understand it to be a rule in dredging contracts that a certain amount has to be charged up to the price for dredging to provide for the plant. If the department simply say :	we will
do no work, or we will ask parliament for $400,000 or $500,000 to get these dredges to do the work in two or three years, and at the end of that time possibly the dredges may not be placed where they can be used, the result will be that a large price must be charged up against the work. But we are gradually adopting a new policy. At the

present time we are building a new dredge on the most approved plans and we hope to be able to accomplish some results with that dredge.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Where is that being built ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: That is being built under contract at the Poison Works in Toronto.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Is it a big dredge ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: It is a 24-inch hydraulic dredge.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Like the 'J. Israel Tarte ' ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Practically on the same principle, except that it has the latest up-to-date improvements in every possible way. The department are gradually trying to get themselves into that position, but I hardly think this House will be prepared to say in the meantime that we should stop all work at Port Arthur.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I know that my hon. friend is not disposed to be unfair ordinarily, but he has given a construction to my remarks which is not in the slightest degree borne out by anything I said. How long have we been dredging in this river ? For several years, have we not ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: For at least thirty years.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Well, we had the announcement made by a responsible minister of the Crown that this work could be done in a very much cheaper way by acquiring dredges and doing the work directly by the department. I do not know whether that can be borne out or not. I was not suggesting that the hon. minister should wait, but I was suggesting that if the policy of the department had at any time been what was thus stated, some inquiry should be made, so that the lion. Minister of Public Works could give some necessary information. The hon. minister says it will not be cheaper, but when I ask him the very questions which are pertinent to the consideration of the subject he is not able to give me any information. He does not know what the cost is of a dredge capable of doing that work. Is not that the first thing to consider in order to come to a conclusion as to whether or not we can do the work more cheaply ourselves ? Would you not have to consider the cost of the dredge and the cost of operation afterwards ?, Would you not have to consider that the dredge during a portion of the time might not be employed after this work has been done ? All these things are proper subjects for consideration, but the hon. minister did not seem to be able to give very much information to the committee. One consideration is, of course, the cost of dredges whicli will be capable of performing this work, and whether or not such dredges can be obtained within a reasonable time. It might turn out, if we had the information, that the hon. minister is exactly right in his conjecture, but the committee should be furnished with the necessary information to enable it to come to a conclusion on the subject, and to offer any suggestions which may seem pertinent before voting the money.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I am sure the hon. gentleman will acquit me of in any possible way desiring to put any unfair construction upon his words. As far as the cost of a dredge is concerned, the committee will quite understand that for in the neighbourhood of $250,000 a first-class suction dredge could be built. That dredge would not do all the work there ; we would require a dredge for hard-pan and rock work, so that we would have to build, in addition to that class of dredge, a dredge which would do hard-pan and rock work.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: These dredges are of more than one class ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: These four dredges are all of one class ;-they are all of the class which is known as the ' dipper ' dredge. I do not think it would be the policy of the department to acquire these dredges. If the government were to acquire and man these dredges themselves, I question very much if the work could be done cheaper than by paying so much for each dredge per hour, or so much per yard for the work under contract. I just wish to say that this dredge question is in Canada a very important and serious one. There are practically no dredges available. I do not know of a single dredge of any capacity which is available in Canada for the works of the department that we are not using. It is a very difficult matter to get dredges, and for that reason I feel convinced that the department must gradually extend this system of buying and manning its own dredges, but I do not believe that the House would agree with the opinion that it would be a proper thing that we should do so in one year.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext:
I sympathize very much with my hon. friend the acting Minister of Public Works. I believe he did not quite catch what the chief of the opposition 1 said. He was not here some years ago, when one of. his predecessors asked parliament for a very large amount of money to equip government works at Sorel. These works were designed for the building of the dredges which will be necessary in Canada. This question was very much discussed here. It was a very large amount of money that was required. Some lion, gentlemen expressed an opinion very much in line with that of my hon. friend, but the majority of the House and the government, who were responsible for it, sustained the opinion of the then Minister of Public Works. The money was spent. I believe

that over half a million dollars was spent at Sorel for the building of a shop there. Am I right in regard to the figure 1

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: It was a large amount, as the hon. gentleman says.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: A good deal of work, in accordance with the intentions of the then minister, was commenced there, but it was not continued. I think this is an evidence of the unfortunate results that follow from the government having no stated policy. If that had been the policy of the government on that subject, whether the Minister of Public Works disappeared or not, that policy should have been continued. It has not been continued. The works at Sorel are not to-day operated to as great an extent as was intended when they were built. I know it may be answered that they are used for repairs for the fleet that is employed in the St. Lawrence channel. That work is not being properly done, if I can judge by what was done last summer, when the boiler on the largest dredge-the ' J. Israel Tarte '-burst, with the result that the dredge could do nothing at all.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.

speechtext: What is the total expenditure ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: This contract is for $179,000 and the only one there at present.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: How long before the work will be finished ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: It was let on June 8, 1904 and should be completed November 30, 1905.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: How does the minister explain an expenditure of $140,000 last year and $150,000 this year ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: There is a typographical error. Part of this is a revote.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Was this in connection with the new harbour, or the ordinary works there ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The harbour, the breakwater and other works going on there.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Is it for the purpose of making the harbour more secure against storms ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: To make the harbour perfectly secure

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: This is simply completing the breakwater. There is work to be carried on under the Department of Railways and Canals in connection with the elevator and the piers.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: According to my recollection, there was dredging to be done-I think some rock had to be taken away. Is that work going on at the same time ? There is little use in carrying on this work if it is not finished to be available for commerce. In view of the rapid changes which sometimes take place in the trade routes, there is danger that this work may be finished too late to be useful.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: There will be some additional work to be done, but, until the work under the Department of Railways and Canals is completed, we cannot say exactly where the dredging work ought to be (carried on.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: If the other work is never done, what will be the advantage of this expenditure ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The other work is being done. The whole is practically one scheme.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: This breakwater will be a shelter for vessels, and will be the completion of a portion of the work.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: In addition, there is work going on in connection with the foundations of the elevators and in other directions. My hon. friend from Lincoln (Mr. Lancaster) lives near the work, and is probably aware of what is being done.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: I know there is work going ou there, but I do not know to what extent.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: Is not this in connection with the two million dollar scheme ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: No ; that is in the other department. This is the breakwater making the harbour.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: What amount of money has been spent on the work, and in what state of advancement is it 7

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: The completion of this will end that part of the work, and it is to be finished, according to the contract, on the 30tli of November next.

speechtext: Who is the contractor ?

ill-. HYMAN. A breakwater 2,400 feet Ibng. which this will complete.

speechtext: Is the dredging under the same department as the building of the breakwater ?

speechtext: Mot up to date. Both the Minister of Public Works and the Minister of Railways and Canals have control of certain of the works in that harbour. Of course, it is not always easy to define where the jurisdiction of one ends and that of the other begins.

speechtext: Can the hon. gentleman tell whether the breakwater is filled in with stone or with concrete ?

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.
speechtext: A timber foundation and a concrete superstructure.

maintopic: DRAWBACKS ON RAW MATERIALS IN THE UNITED STATES TARIFF-SUPPLY.

Would it not be a saving to use the stone taken from the bottom to fill in the breakwater, instead of hauling it for miles to get rid of it and hauling other stone for miles to fill in with?

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE.
speechtext: Will the minister tell us what business we may expect tomorrow ?

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE.
speechtext: If there are any Bills ready, we will proceed with them. When those orders are exhausted, I suppose we shall go on with supply, taking up, until six o'clock, the estimates of the Minister of Public Works, and after that the estimates of the Department of Trade and Commerce.
